title: Gold Loans Surge: What RBI's Financial Stability Report Reveals
description: Gold loans are now India's fastest-growing retail credit segment, as per the latest RBI Financial Stability Report (FSR). They have shown a remarkable Compoun.

faq.q: What is the RBI Financial Stability Report (FSR)?
faq.a: The RBI FSR is a half-yearly report published by the Reserve Bank of India that assesses the health and resilience of the Indian financial system, identifying potential risks and vulnerabilities.

faq.q: Why are gold loans growing so fast?
faq.a: Gold loans are growing rapidly due to their easy accessibility, quick disbursement, lower interest rates compared to unsecured loans, and flexible repayment options, appealing to those needing immediate funds.

faq.q: Is my gold safe with the lender?
faq.a: Reputable banks and NBFCs take extensive measures to ensure the safety and security of pledged gold, typically storing it in secure vaults and providing insurance coverage. Always choose a regulated entity.

faq.q: What happens if I can't repay a gold loan?
faq.a: If you fail to repay a gold loan, the lender has the right to auction your pledged gold to recover the outstanding loan amount. This can result in the permanent loss of your gold.

faq.q: Are gold loans cheaper than personal loans?
faq.a: Generally, yes. Gold loans are secured loans, meaning they are backed by collateral (gold), which reduces the risk for the lender. This allows them to offer lower interest rates compared to unsecured personal loans.

faq.q: Can NRIs take gold loans in India?
faq.a: Yes, NRIs can typically take gold loans in India, often through NRE/NRO accounts. However, the specific terms, documentation, and eligibility criteria can vary between lenders.

faq.q: Does taking a gold loan affect my credit score?
faq.a: A gold loan is a secured loan and generally has less impact on your credit score than an unsecured loan. However, timely repayment can positively contribute to your credit history, while defaults can negatively affect it.
